items.title: Are dividends an overlooked path to long-term wealth?
items.summary: The Bahnsen Group CIO, David Bahnsen, talks with Market Domination's Josh Lipton about how dividend growth investing can build long-term wealth and outperform inflation. Bahnsen emphasizes that young investors benefit from a dividend growth strategy because of its compounding potential.

items.title: The 30-Year U.S. Treasury Bond Now Has a Higher Yield Than Ford and Coca-Cola. Is It Now the Best Asset for Passive Income?
items.summary: The yield on the 30-year U.S. Treasury bond has surged past 5.2% and, not too long ago, had surpassed 5.3%.

items.title: 5 Blue-Chip Dividend Stocks to Buy Before August Ends
items.summary: August's final days are closing a narrow window for income investors, and five blue-chip names with multi-decade dividend streaks just posted earnings beats that change the calculus on each one.

items.title: 2 Dividend Stocks to Buy and Hold for Long-Term Safety and Income
items.summary: These two consumer staples have outperformed the market in 2026 and still offer high yields.

items.title: Celsius Stock: Can A New Growth Engine Outrun A Stumble In Its Core Brand?
items.summary: The energy drink maker is posting impressive portfolio growth, but a self-admitted misstep with its flagship brand creates a sharp question for anyone buying today.

items.title: Coca-Cola Is No Longer Just a Dividend Stock
items.summary: Five straight earnings beats and a 35% one-year rally have investors questioning whether KO still belongs in the dividend stock category, and the answer reshapes how you should value it today.

items.title: Coca-Cola vs. PepsiCo: Which Stock Deserves the Top Spot in Beverages?
items.summary: KO's beverage ecosystem, global reach, brand strength and earnings growth highlight its fundamentals, while PEP's diversified drinks and foods portfolio supports consumer reach.

items.title: Pepsi vs. Coke: One Stock Is Starting to Pull Ahead
items.summary: Coke and Pepsi both reported Q2 earnings this week, but their results told completely different stories about brand power, margin strength, and where consumer spending is actually heading.
